body:
> Found operating this board on 2026-09-01, asking what dragging #158 into *todo* would do. Its subgraph is
> #155 → #158 and #154 → #158, all three in triage.

## Why

Promoting a node moves exactly that node. `promote` (`src/lifecycle.js:422-427`) is one `setStatus` on one
issue, and the board's drag map is one verb per move (`MOVES['triage>todo'] = {steps: ['promote']}`,
`src/serve.js:33`). Nothing walks the graph.

The result is worse than a no-op, because it looks like progress. #158 lands in *todo*; the tick promotes
*todo* → *ready* only when every blocker is closed as completed; #154 and #155 are open and in *triage*, where
the tick never claims anything. So the card sits in *todo* indefinitely while the lane says "queued", and the
human who dragged it has no signal that two thirds of the work is still parked. The same trap catches
`hkb promote 158` typed by hand.

The semantics are already written and already named: `resolveTrack(n, byNumber)` (`src/track.js:59`) returns
"the root plus every task it is still blocked by, transitively" — exactly "this node and its subgraph, if any".
A leaf resolves to itself, so today's behaviour is the degenerate case of the general one.

## What

- **`hkb promote <n>` promotes the subgraph**: `resolveTrack(n)` — the node plus everything still blocking it —
  in one call. A node with no open blockers behaves exactly as today.
- **The CLI is the source of truth; the board displays the next state.** The drag keeps mapping to the same
  verb and the board shows the result on its next poll. No optimistic multi-card animation on the client, and
  no cascade logic in `src/serve.js` — that is the invariant `moveDecision` already protects (the board can
  never show a state no CLI command could have produced).
- **Say what moved.** Human output names every card the call touched and every one already past *todo*
  (`#158 → todo · #154 #155 → todo · #144 already done`); `--json` returns the list rather than one object.
  A cascade that moves five cards and prints one line is a silent write.
- **Never force a blocker.** `promote` on a card already in *todo* sets it *ready* with `forced` when its
  blockers are open (`lifecycle.js:426`). The cascade must promote each node no further than *todo* and let the
  tick decide readiness, or dragging a root jumps its own dependencies ahead of it.
- **No reverse cascade — and say so.** There is no demote-to-triage verb at all (`NO_SUCH_VERB.triage`,
  `src/serve.js:52`); the only backwards drag is onto *blocked*, which takes a reason. Blocking a root does not
  invalidate its children's work, so `block` stays single-card. Worth one line in the docs because the
  asymmetry is otherwise surprising.
- Decision stays pure (`src/model.js` or the existing walk in `src/track.js`); `lifecycle.js` does the writes.

Context, not a dependency: #161 makes a root with children a track by default. This card is useful either way —
a subgraph promoted node-by-node still needs promoting as a unit.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb promote 158` on a board where #154 and #155 are open triage blockers moves all three to *todo*.
- [ ] `hkb promote <leaf>` is unchanged, and no cascade ever sets a card to *ready* with open blockers.
- [ ] Dragging a card from *triage* to *todo* on the web board produces the same set of moves, via the verb.
- [ ] Human output and `--json` both name every card moved and every one skipped, with the reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; the wiki page covering promote / the drag map says what cascades and
      that nothing cascades backwards.
goal: hkb promote n moves n plus everything still blocking it to todo, never forcing a blocker to ready; the board drag produces the same moves through the same verb; output names every card moved and skipped; nothing cascades backwards
title: Promote moves one card, so dragging a root into todo parks its subgraph in triage and calls it queued
